summary: Confirmed and pinned the exact supported Jellyfin 12.0.0 item-image publication/read ABI, the standard Jellyfin.Api ImageController route variants, the read/write authorization split, and Jellyfin's ownership of image tags, caching, and resizing. Publication surface: MediaBrowser.Controller.Providers.IProviderManager.SaveImage with the stream overload Task SaveImage(BaseItem, Stream, string, ImageType, int?, CancellationToken) plus the URL (string url) and filesystem-path (string source, string mimeType, ..., bool? saveLocallyWithMedia) overloads; the path overload deletes its source file. Read/information surface: BaseItem.GetImageInfo(ImageType, int) -> MediaBrowser.Controller.Entities.ItemImageInfo, BaseItem.ImageInfos, MediaBrowser.Model.Dto.ImageInfo (ImageTag/Width/Height/Size), IImageProcessor.GetImageCacheTag (MD5 of item path + image modified ticks in 12.0.0; a cache validator, not a content hash), IImageProcessor.GetImageDimensions, and ILibraryManager.UpdateImagesAsync/ConvertImageToLocal/GetItemById<T>. Repository update: BaseItem.UpdateToRepositoryAsync(ItemUpdateType, CancellationToken) with ItemUpdateType.ImageUpdate = 4. Types: ImageType in MediaBrowser.Model.Entities (Primary = 0, ...), ImageFormat in MediaBrowser.Model.Drawing, ItemImageInfo in MediaBrowser.Controller.Entities, ImageInfo in MediaBrowser.Model.Dto. Routes (pinned from the host Jellyfin.Api.dll and its OpenAPI): Items/{itemId}/Images/{imageType} (GET/HEAD), Items/{itemId}/Images/{imageType}/{imageIndex} (GET/HEAD), Items/{itemId}/Images/{imageType}/{imageIndex}/{tag}/{format}/{maxWidth}/{maxHeight}/{percentPlayed}/{unplayedCount} (GET/HEAD), Items/{itemId}/Images (GET), and the POST/DELETE write routes. Delivery (confirmed from the pinned source/artifact): a tag query yields a quoted ETag and Cache-Control public max-age=31536000 immutable with If-None-Match 304 handling; without a tag Cache-Control public and If-Modified-Since; Jellyfin never upscales (DrawingUtils.ScaleDownToFit); the sealed Jellyfin.Drawing.ImageProcessor owns the resized-images cache. Authorization: the GET/HEAD item-image read actions carry no [Authorize] attribute; they resolve the item through _libraryManager.GetItemById<BaseItem>(itemId, User.GetUserId()), where an anonymous request's empty user id (ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.GetUserId() returns default(Guid)) maps to a null user and LibraryManager.ItemIsVisible(item, null) returns true for any non-null item. A known item's image is therefore served anonymously (HTTP 200); only an unknown item id (or an item with no image of the requested type) yields 404. The item-image information action and all write actions carry [Authorize]/[Authorize(Policy = RequiresElevation)]. The route/authorization status observations are live-confirmed on the pinned host, and the pinned host OpenAPI document shows security=null for the GET/HEAD item-image operations. Later tasks must not assume a 401 from the read image route or treat it as an authorization boundary. V1 remains the unindexed Primary poster for Movie and Episode only (ADR-006/ADR-009); indexed/alternate poster surfaces are out of V1. Findings recorded in docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 4.4 (route table in 3.1, response/authorization behavior in 3.3). Added an unguarded ABI test (JellyfinImageAbiTests, 11 cases reflecting the pinned NuGet assemblies) and a host-guarded route/authorization test (JellyfinImageRouteTests, 5 cases reflecting the pinned host Jellyfin.Api.dll via ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR). No ADR, RenderVersion, renderer, or publication behavior was changed; no Phase 5 implementation was added.

Reflection probes confirmed the exact signatures, enum values, and type namespaces from the pinned assemblies.

Reflection over the pinned host Jellyfin.Api.dll confirmed all ImageController route templates, action names, verbs, and Authorize attributes; the pinned host's generated OpenAPI document showed security=null for the GET/HEAD item-image operations while GetItemImageInfos and all POST/DELETE operations require CustomAuthentication.

Live pinned-host probes confirmed route/authorization status observations: an anonymous GET /Items/{unknown-id}/Images/Primary reached the action and returned 404 for the unknown id, GET /Items/{id}/Images and POST /Items/{id}/Images/Primary returned 401, an invalid imageType returned 400, and a control GET /Items/{id} returned 401. Per the reviewer correction, the 404 reflected the unknown item id, not a visibility-based rejection: an anonymous request maps to a null user and a known item's image is served anonymously (200). The test host was stopped afterwards.

known_limitations: The five JellyfinImageRouteTests cases require ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR because Jellyfin.Api.dll is a host application assembly, not a NuGet package referenced by the test project. They are reported as skipped in the default ./build.sh test run and pass 5/5 when the variable points at the pinned host. The ABI signature tests are unguarded and always run.

The ABI and route templates are confirmed from the pinned artifacts; the exact on-disk representation SaveImage produces for the selected host configuration and the post-publication read-back content hash remain host-behavior validation for later Phase 5 tasks (ADR-002/ADR-003), not ABI uncertainty. The stream overload has no saveLocallyWithMedia parameter and follows the library's SaveLocalMetadata option; only the filesystem-path overload exposes bool? saveLocallyWithMedia, and that overload deletes its source file.

Corrected behavior (reviewer F1): the GET/HEAD item-image read actions carry no method-level [Authorize] and are NOT visibility-rejected for anonymous callers. An anonymous request's empty user id maps to a null user and ItemIsVisible(item, null) returns true for any non-null item, so a known item's image is served anonymously (HTTP 200); only an unknown item id (or an item with no image of the requested type) yields 404. The pinned OpenAPI shows security=null for these operations. Later Phase 5 tasks must not assume a 401 from the read image route or treat it as an authorization boundary; it does not change the ADR-001 decision to use the standard route.

No live host was used to publish a derived image in this task; the live host was used only to confirm route/authorization status observations, and its generated OpenAPI document independently corroborated the route security metadata. The cache-header/ETag/Last-Modified and never-upscale resize behavior are confirmed from the pinned source/artifact, not measured live (reviewer F2). Task scope was limited to confirming the ABI; no publication, provenance, host source adapter, packaging, journal, reconciliation, lifecycle, or Enhanced-coexistence work was implemented.
